canonical_concepts.label: BADMINTON
definitions: a racket sport played by either two opposing players (singles) or two opposing pairs (doubles).
The sport was then known as 'The Game of Badminton' for a number of years, until the name was shortened to BADMINTON.

canonical_concepts.label: badminton court
definitions: a rectangular area divided by a net.
A court marked for both singles and doubles matches, rectangular and divided into halves by a net.

canonical_concepts.label: shuttlecock
definitions: A projectile with an open conical shape.
An object used in the game that is hit back and forth over a net.

canonical_concepts.label: net
definitions: The net is 1.55 m high.

canonical_concepts.label: Poona
definitions: A form of badminton played in colonial India.

canonical_concepts.label: Badminton rackets
definitions: Badminton rackets are light, with top quality rackets weighting between 79 and 91 grams including the strings.

canonical_concepts.label: Synthetic shuttles
section_paths: 1. Scoring system: 3 x 21 rally point scoring system.

canonical_concepts.label: singles court
definitions: A court that is 5.18 meters wide and 13.40 meters long.
The area where the server and receiver must stand during the serve.
A court that is narrower than the doubles court but the same length (with the service exception).

canonical_concepts.label: Defensive clear
definitions: A wider court than the singles court, with a shorter serve-length dimension.

canonical_concepts.label: rally
definitions: A sequence of shots in which players hit the shuttlecock back and forth.
A continuous exchange of hits between players until a point is won or lost.
section_paths: 1. Scoring system: 3 x 21 rally point scoring system.

canonical_concepts.label: game
definitions: A segment of play where players compete to reach 21 points with a margin of at least two points.
section_paths: 1. Scoring system: 3 x 21 rally point scoring system.

canonical_concepts.label: match
definitions: A competition consisting of the best of three games.
section_paths: 1. Scoring system: 3 x 21 rally point scoring system.

canonical_concepts.label: feints
definitions: Deceptive movements by the server to disconcert the opponent.

canonical_concepts.label: fault
definitions: An action that results in losing the rally, such as hitting the shuttlecock into the net or out of bounds.

canonical_concepts.label: Service
definitions: Under waist shot.

canonical_concepts.label: Drive service
definitions: Upper arm or overhead shot - hitting the shuttle so that it falls softly downwards into the opponents' forecourt, very close to the net.

canonical_concepts.label: Clear
definitions: Upper arm or overhead shot - hitting the shuttle high and to the back of the opponents' court, the rearcourt.

canonical_concepts.label: Smash
definitions: Upper arm or overhead shot – hitting the shuttle downwards and fast, attempting to win the rally immediately. It is also called 'kill'.

canonical_concepts.label: Drive
definitions: Hitting the shuttle as far as you can, not too high, horizontally and fast.

canonical_concepts.label: Hairpin net shot
definitions: Under arm shot - hitting the shuttle softly back to the net.

canonical_concepts.label: Lob
definitions: Under arm shot – hitting the shuttle high and to the back of the opponents’ court.

canonical_concepts.label: teamwork
definitions: the success formula in doubles

canonical_concepts.label: HOME POSITION
definitions: a position in the midcourt area where you can possibly reach any of your opponent's shots

canonical_concepts.label: FOUR CORNERS STRATEGY
definitions: Always try to hit the shuttle away from your opponent and make your opponent move around the court.

canonical_concepts.label: WIDE VARIETY OF STROKES
definitions: Using different types of strokes depending on the situation to be flexible.
